newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian railway standards lagging, minister says.
newsitem.headline: Italian railway standards lagging, minister says.

text.p: Transport Minister Claudio Burlando, under attack following two rail accidents over the weekend, said on Monday that Italy's trains were safe, but added that the domestic railway network fell well behind European standards.
"The ratio between accidents and victims is one of the lowest in Europe," Burlando said in an interview with La Repubblica newspaper.
"(But) Italy's railway system faces an infrastructural and technological delay that has perhaps no equal in Europe."

Rail travel throughout Italy was thrown into chaos after a passenger train derailed in Rome on Saturday and then a crane working to remove the train collapsed onto four tracks that make up the main rail artery connecting north and south.
Passengers suffered minor injuries in Saturday's derailment and trains were delayed for up to 12 hours, leaving thousands of travellers stranded, as engineers struggled to clear the tracks.

Union leaders and members of the centre-right parliamentary opposition bloc heaped criticism onto Burlando and railway officials, with the far-right party National Alliance demanding the minister's resignation.
Rail travel was still disrupted on Monday, with only one of the four blocked tracks operating.
Asked in the interview how long it would take Italy's railways to match those of other European countries, Burlando said:
"Two years for the introduction of the automatic traffic control system on the main lines and five years for the quadrupling of the tracks connecting north and south."
He said the government had already set aside funds for a restructuring of the rail system, which included a four-fold extension of the number of tracks that go from north to south.
"We face terrible delays with regard to the renovation of the railway system...In other European countries these systems have already been adopted."
Eight people died last January when a Milan-Rome high speed train derailed near the northern city of Piacenza.
Investigators suspected excess speed caused that accident and newspapers reported that Saturday's derailment might also have been caused by speed limits being broken.
